texts.text:
Greetings, $N,

You've shown great promise as a $c, and I'd like to ensure that you receive proper guidance and training. 

The rangers do a good job of keeping the wilds in check here in Thendal Grove, but beyond our borders... well, the same can't be said.

Come find me near the center of the village as soon as you are able. The wilds are calling.

-Tai'ree Farsight, $C Trainer

The cult hit us by surprise. Raani never saw it coming and Arvensus took a sword to the gut. For my part, I took a lightning bolt to the chest and blacked out. They never bothered to finish me off... I guess they assumed my wounds would do me in. When it's all said and done, I suspect they might.

As soon as the fighting stopped, they started moving massive crates of windstones to the top of the tower. The leader, some kind of priest, said something about a ritual.

I'm writing this note just in case I don't make it back to Shen'dar to warn Aonda, but they are doing something here. Something bad.

If anyone finds this, please, do your best to stop them. There were only a few left at the tower when I scribbled this note and crawled away.

Also, try and get Raani's lucky feather from his body. He liked to tell tall tales about how he plucked it from some kind of firebird and I think he'd want to make sure that it made its way back home.

If you are also able to retrieve Arvensus Shadowsong's family signet from his body, please do so. High Elder Shadowsong is his uncle and he would want it to be returned to the family.

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"An excerpt from the Shal'nan's speech at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Shrine of the Four Winds, Zephras Isle."

"With the founding of our new home here in the clouds, we embark on a new age of peace and prosperity for our people.

You have all endured so much to make it here. I have watched our people grow into a hardy, self-reliant society, which fills me with a pride I cannot hope to describe in full.

The greatest part of that pride, however, is that it has become clear to me that I no longer have any need to act as our singular ruler."

"Thus, I am abdicating my position as your leader and handing over governance of our Skyborne Isles to a carefully chosen council of provincial elders. After the transition period is over, you will have the opportunity to choose your own leaders, and your voices will determine the direction we take from here on. 

You have demonstrated the ability to lead yourselves better than any king, queen, prince, or other individual sovereign ever could--and that fills me with profound pride."

"I will continue to serve our people here on Zephras, and I will devote much of my time to furthering our relationship with the wind spirits to whom we owe so much. The elemental spirits are wondrous and wise, and we still have so much to learn from one another.

I am devoted to seeing the shen'dorei persevere in this beautiful and strange realm--and to seeing that we do so freely, justly, and unshackled by tyranny."

"Thank you for everything you've sacrificed, everything you've built, and everything you've taught me about how to be a better person. You all represent the unshakable resolve of the shen'dorei people. We will thrive in this beautiful new world and reach new heights together."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 1"

"In the days immediately following the turmoil at the Well of Eternity, there was much unrest in Eldre'Thalas. The demonic forces that poured from the Well nearly overwhelmed the beleaguered elvish kingdoms, ravaging the land and killing indiscriminately. If not for the intervention of the demigod Goldrinn and the sacrifice of countless kaldorei heroes, the kingdom of Eldre'Thalas would surely have been overrun and destroyed."

"After the climax of the war and the Great Sundering of Kalimdor, the new reality of a world bereft of the sustaining magic on which our people depended quickly became apparent. The ruling house of Eldre'Thalas--House Tortheldrin--rapidly set plans in motion to ensure stability and continuity of our way of life. However, the methods they intended to employ left many deeply concerned."

"The young Prince Tortheldrin intended to build a network of crystalline foci and use them to siphon and shape a new font of power for our people to draw upon. The point of contention for many was that he intended to use the very power that nearly destroyed our world to accomplish this. He meant to siphon this power from a demon world within the Twisting Nether itself. 

Many rightly feared this could open a new door through which demonic entities might gain once again access to our world."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 2"

"There were those who loudly opposed the Prince's plan to channel a font of demonic energy to power his network of crystalline foci. Many of the detractors were members of outspoken noble families who attempted to use their influence to turn public sentiment against House Tortheldrin and the Prince's plan."

"Prince Tortheldrin grew frustrated, fearing that delays and debate would lead to the further deterioration of his kingdom. 

As a result, his response to this resistance was swift and brutal. Over the course of a single bloody night, a purge was carried out that saw the complete destruction of dozens of noble houses. All who publicly opposed Tortheldrin were abruptly silenced, and entire lineages were destroyed overnight."

"The terror of such brazen suppression caused a shocked silence to fall over the people of Eldre'Thalas. All discourse around Prince Tortheldrin's plan abruptly ceased... for a time, at least. Unfortunately for the Prince, the harder tyrants squeeze their people, the brighter the flames of resistance burn.

There were those who resolved to ensure our people did not repeat Queen Azshara's mistakes. A group of scholars formerly of the order of the Shen'dralar met in secret and formed a pact. Swearing to stop the Prince by any means necessary, they began to plant the seeds of rebellion."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 3"

"The leader of the rebels was a mysterious figure known only as the 'Shal'nan' or, 'The Veiled One.' He wore a featureless golden mask intended to conceal his identity and protect those close to him. This man quickly became a symbol for ordinary citizens who would stand up against oppression, and the word Shal'nan became a battle cry synonymous with rebellion.

Through sabotage, coercion, and--according to some rumors--assassination, the rebels quickly became a thorn in the side of Prince Tortheldrin's efforts to construct his network of crystalline foci."

"The message of resistance spread by the Shal'nan began to gain traction within Eldre'Thalas, due in no small part to the very public embarrassment the Prince suffered nearly daily at the hands of rebel operations.

Awareness of an alternative, more naturalistic way of life also spread quickly in the kingdom at this time. This was heavily influenced by the example set by the Cenarion druids, who had taken control of the greater kaldorei empire in the northern part of the continent. There were even rumors that the rebels were secretly supported by covert agents sent by the new de facto leader of the night elves: the Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage."

"The Prince railed against the idea of an alternative path to combat his people's dependence on magic. He claimed that calls to embrace naturalistic magic were propaganda spread by illegitimate usurpers to Queen Azshara's vacant throne. 

He and his supporters dismissed druidic magic as base and barbaric--utterly beneath the proud, ancient traditions of the highborne. Yet the practice of druidism began to take hold on the fringes of Eldre'Thalas society, and with it, the rebellion continued to grow."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 4"

"On the eve of the planned summoning ritual, the Shal'nan and his forces struck. Seeing this as their final opportunity to thwart Prince Tortheldrin's reckless plan, they made a daring raid on the Prince's sanctum, intent on stopping the ritual.

Just as the Shal'nan and the rebels feared, the poorly considered spell spiraled out of control and threatened to destroy the entire city center. 

As the battle raged, wild magics tore through the streets, opening portals to the Nether itself and manifesting malevolent arcane monstrosities that preyed mercilessly upon the defenseless citizens of Eldre'Thalas."

"In the end, the worst of the destruction was narrowly avoided due to the rebels' intervention, but the price was steep. The battle claimed many lives on all sides, but the rebels suffered the greatest losses. 

The Shal'nan himself was the only one to survive the final confrontation within Tortheldrin's sanctum. Those closest to the Shal'nan have widely documented that whatever injury he suffered in that last battle left him forever changed. In the centuries since those dark days, the Shal'nan has never spoken of what occurred, and he becomes withdrawn and wistful when asked."

"In the immediate aftermath of the battle, Tortheldrin's forces were scattered and disorganized. Most were occupied with securing the city once more, and this distraction allowed the remaining rebels to escape and regroup. With nowhere else to go, the Shal'nan marched what was left of his exhausted forces west, toward the coast."

"When the beleaguered rebel army arrived at the port city of Eldre'narr, the magisters in control of the city had already heard of Tortheldrin's mighty rage--and of his standing order to kill any rebel found on sight. In an act of miraculous mercy, the magisters made no move to hinder the rebels' progress, allowing them to commandeer a number of ships without resistance.

The Shal'nan understood that this act of mercy would likely expose many in Eldre'narr to Tortheldrin's wrath. Even so, he accepted this unexpected gift with grace and, with a heavy heart, sailed his people west into the unknown."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"On The Windlord."

"Who is Al'Akir the Windlord? The priests of the radical Al'Aketh would have us believe him to be the true ruler of Skywall, the realm we now call home. In their telling, we are but interlopers here, and one day Al'Akir shall appear before us to reckon with our trespass into his dominion within the elemental plane.

Though such claims may at first seem the ravings of the misguided or the mad, there may yet be some measure of truth in them. When asked of Al'Akir's nature, the wind spirits grow evasive and agitated. Indeed, even the mere speaking of the so-called "Windlord's" name appears to cause them profound unease, perhaps even fear."

"Whatever the truth may be, our benefactors clearly have no wish to speak of Al'Akir or his servants, and they are quick to dismiss all rumors of the Windlord's presence as idle fancy, unworthy of serious heed. They assure us that we need not trouble ourselves with such matters here, safe upon our Skyborne Isles. While this offers solemn comfort to many, it also raises a troubling question: what, precisely, are the wind spirits concealing from us?"

"Of late, the magisters of the High Order have grown increasingly wary of the wind spirits' motives, insisting that all powers and perils native to this realm must be better understood. Even if such dangers lie far from us now, the magisters maintain that such knowledge will better prepare us to face whatever may yet come."

"The skyseer elders among the Windshapers, by contrast, place implicit trust in the wind spirits and regard any questioning of their designs as an affront to our benefactors. They hold that our patrons in Skywall have already sacrificed much to bring us here and sustain us. They assert that if any further knowledge was vital to our survival, they would surely reveal it in due course. This difference in belief has given rise to no small measure of tension between the two orders.

Whatever the truth may be, it is plain that we are not alone in this realm, and that many mysteries yet remain beyond our present understanding."

King Llane I of the House of Wrynn

Liege Lord of Stormwind 

Defender of Azeroth

npc:11044.text: Once, it is true, I was human. What might otherwise be a shortcoming works to our advantage, $n, for I know human weaknesses intimately.

npc:1300.text: Life is like a carefully woven tapestry.

npc:1314.text: I sell only the finest arcane gear, made by the crafters and mages here in the city of Stormwind.

npc:1346.text: Yes, I've been running this shop for some time now. Business has been pretty good lately. A lot of new adventurers coming through...

npc:1347.text: Since the fall of Dalaran and the destruction of Quel'Thalas, wares of this sort have been hard to come by. But Lucan Cordell and some of our other Tradesman have been doing a fine job of filling our orders with quality merchandise.

npc:14722.text: Friend - Stormwind needs your assistance and your generosity!$B$BOur once large stockpile of textiles has run critically low.  Stormwind is now engaged in a multi-pronged effort to rebuild those stocks for the manufacture of textiles and bandages!  Your donation of cloth would help Stormwind immensely, as well as earn the respect of the citizenry!

npc:14729.text: You there... it is in your best interest to aid the Forsaken during these dire times.  Listen closely, as I dislike repeating myself.$B$BWe currently find ourselves in a dire shortage of cloth.  Bandages and simple textiles are running low, and donations are being accepted to bolster sagging inventories.  While you'll not receive financial compensation - hence what donation means - your aid will not go unnoticed.

npc:1937.text: The Dark Lady has put the challenge forth. Now it is up to the Royal Apothecary Society to develop a new plague. We shall bring Arthas and his wretched army to their knees.

npc:2127.text: It is wise that you humble yourself before me $n in your desire for more warlock knowledge.

npc:2132.text: Nice to see a friendly face. I don't get much chitchat from Apothecary Johaan unless he wants something. He's been out of the grave too long. Someday I'll be like that, I hear. Creepy. Maybe by then I won't care.

npc:2226.text: Greetings.  Our bats are well trained and fed.  You'll not find faster.

npc:2425.text: Do not presume to speak to me as though you are my equal, $c. Sylvanas is my queen, and I will do as she bids.$B$BIf you do not show the proper respect, I assure you, we can find a more than suitable place for you in the Nether.$B$BBut there is no reason we cannot have words if you wish to aid the Dark Lady...

npc:246389.text:
Why do they call me "The Breaker"?

Trust me, you don't want to know.

npc:249363.text:
The Wind Spirits have left us. 

Now, only mindless echoes remain. Be wary, however. These winds are neither kind, nor gentle.

npc:2504.text: Please clean yourself before handling our tomes.

npc:250686.text: Praise to the Banshee Queen, it isn't often I have visitors out here.

npc:250929.text: <As you approach the enormous cyclone construct, you hear a faint buzzing emanating from beneath its massive armor plates. If you listen carefully, you think you might be able to hear a few words being formed but they are too distorted to make out.>

npc:251361.text: What do you need of me, child of Zephras?

npc:251371.text: Greetings to you, fellow High Order initiate.

Magic can accomplish almost anything, but stagnation and inaction have caused us to lose so much of ourselves in the thousands of years since we left Kalimdor. The High Order seeks to reclaim the Highborne heritage that we've left behind and become the masters of our own destiny once again.

The Windshapers think we are simply reckless and arrogant. Hypocrisy at its finest, if you ask me. The Windshapers will entertain no ideas but their own when it comes to this crisis. Who, I wonder, is truly arrogant?

Zephras is in great danger. The elemental wind spirits that brought us here to Skywall so many thousands of years ago have abandoned us, leaving us vulnerable in this unstable realm. Our once-robust society spanned multiple island sanctuaries in our corner of Skywall, but now we are not even sure if any other shen'dorei remain outside of this small island.

Things are dire, but the High Order is committed to rising to this challenge.

npc:251376.text:
The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.

npc:251389.text:
Slay your enemies and swoon your paramours with this one weird trick.

If you follow the path of the rogue, I can teach you... for a cost, of course.

npc:251487.text:
I can tell by your aura that you are of highborne lineage, yes? Those that call themselves members of the High Order find very little common ground with the members of my order, the Windshapers. Outside the relative harmony of Thendal Grove, you may find that these divisions run very deep, deep enough to drive division and even violence.

Be mindful of this as you move throughout Zephras Isle. I'll offer you this one warning... do not cross the Windshapers.

The shen'dorei will always owe the spirits a debt for their aid, and the Windshapers have sworn an oath to repay that debt and restore things to the way they were before. Unfortunately, we are dangerously blind to what is happening around us within Skywall without the spirits to guide us.

The High Order are shortsighted and arrogant, just like their highborne ancestors. They seek to master and control the magic of this place. This is the very path that led us to flee from Kalimdor and reside here in the first place. I fear that much like our forebears their confidence has vastly outpaced their competence and the end result could be disastrous.

Zephras is in a state of decline, unfortunately. The elemental wind spirits that brought us here to Skywall so many thousands of years ago have vanished, causing us to lose much of the magic on which we've depended for millennia.

The island itself is also dangerously unstable, and we've even lost contact with the other island provinces of the shen'dorei. The few Windshapers that still possess the gift of skysight have attempted to contact our brothers and sisters on the other islands, but we have had no response.

Many among us are worried that the shen'dorei here on Zephras are all that is left of our people.

npc:251523.text: <Constable Aonda wears an intense look on her face, clearly deep in thought.>

More than I'd like, I'm afraid. We've been harassed by a group of bandits camping out in a cave to the north, and the Al'Aketh cult recently took over Falaath Village to the south of us. I trust every peacekeeper and citizen here, but we are far too few to keep the village secure. 

If the cult decides to continue their expansion here, there's little we can do to stop them.

npc:251903.text:
Hello there, young $c. I am Rathiril Sunlance and I am an elder Magister of the High Order here on Zephras Isle. It's always good to see bright-eyed young shen'dorei, ready to do their duty in service to their homeland.

Don't let this dusty old mage hold you up, however. No doubt you've got many adventures to see to. Feel free to stop by later if you'd like to speak more.

npc:251904.text: Greetings, $c. Do you come seeking the blessings of the Windlord?

npc:251905.text: If you need training as a cook, I have a few tips and tricks I could pass on! Ho ho! Throw on an apron and let's get started!

Ho there, traveler! New to town? Well, once you get settled in, come see me if you'd like some work. I've been working overtime preparing for the Festival of Winds and I'll take all the help I can get keeping the larders full!

npc:251906.text: I'm in charge of Shen'dar Village operations, and there's a lot of things to keep track of around here. Between bandits, cultists, and other random incidents that pop up, keeping this village afloat is a lot of work.

npc:251913.text: I can teach you to swing a blacksmith's hammer, if you are willing to learn.

npc:251964.text: The warrior who flinches is the warrior who dies. If you would look death in the face as a warrior, I will teach you how not to flinch.

npc:251968.text:
<Ayessa Dawnsinger eyes you with barely-contained fury.> 

You are either very bold, or very stupid to so brazenly step foot into our domain after spilling Windshaper blood. We are slow to forgive, and we never forget. 

You should remove yourself from here at once. If we weren't in the center of Zephras, you would already be dead.

Hmm, I see. Very well then, $c. The Windshapers will provide aid. Please inform Valennia that she can count on us for this fight.

<Ayessa lowers her voice dangerously.> 

Do not mistake our cooperation for any sort of forgiveness. You owe the Windshapers blood, and someday we will collect.

npc:251991.text:
The clothcraft of the Shen'dorei is a harmonious imitation of the flowing, carefree currents of the winds. While the spirits have left us, and I know not when I may see them dance once more... I find great comfort in my art, if only as a distraction.

I can teach you to work the cloth as well, if you'd like to learn?

npc:251993.text: I can teach you to craft fine leather armor, if you have the aptitude.

npc:252155.text: <The corpse lying before you is covered in scorches and burn marks. He seems to be clutching something in his hand.>

npc:252359.text: Our kind are rare these days, but there are those who still dream in emerald amongst the Shen'dorei.

npc:252377.text: The warrior who flinches is the warrior who dies. If you would look death in the face as a warrior, I will teach you how not to flinch.

If you follow the path of the rogue, I can teach you... for a cost, of course.

npc:252383.text:
<Valennia looks away briefly before looking hesitantly back in your direction.>

The Shal'nan was the very best of us. It was he who stood up for our people against madness and oppression in Eldre'Thalas nearly ten thousand years ago. It was the Shal'nan who led us across the uncharted sea to escape the murderous vengeance of our ancient enemies.

It was the Shal'nan who brokered the pact of friendship with the wind spirits that allowed us to ascend to Skywall... and survive.

He was ever the servant leader to his people, even after he abdicated his position of power and retired.

I might be the only living shen'dorei left amongst our people who had more than a handful of words with him.

I served him as the captain of his Empyrean Blades for nearly nine centuries, right up until... he left us.

Even still, I can't rightly claim that I "knew" him. He was ever a reserved and solitary man. He spent most of his time alone or in communion with the spirits in the spires high above the Shrine of the Four Winds... the place that the cult now calls the 'Shrine of Akir'.

I suppose that is true. I and the rest of my elites used to belong to an order known as the Empyrean Blades. We were the personal guard of our former leader, the Shal'nan. 

In the current, uncertain times we do what we can to help lead the peacekeepers' citizen militia, since we are the closest thing to professional soldiers left on Zephras.

If I knew that then I suspect that life here on Zephras would be much, much easier. So many of our struggles and conflicts revolve around that very mystery.

I appreciate your curiosity on this matter but I'm afraid that is all I have to say about this for today.

The Peacekeepers can't hope to muster the numbers needed for an outright assault on the shrine. Without the Windshapers and the High Order bolstering our numbers, we stand no chance. They both pledged their aid when we need it. Now is the time.

Unfortunately, some recent events have led to outright bloodshed between the two factions, and tensions are high.

How do you feel about a bit of diplomacy?

npc:252392.text:
Greetings, young $c. Welcome to the hall of the Tradesman's Guild. Resources are tight on Zephras right now, but you should be able to find a variety of materials and wares here to keep you in top adventuring form.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

npc:252448.text: <The man lying before you shifts uncomfortably. He's recovering from some very nasty wounds.>
It's always great to see you, $n.

npc:252475.text: Greetings, I am Elaadrin Evengale, the current Supreme Magister of the High Order. How can I help you?

I see. This seems dangerous in the extreme, but the situation seems to demand that risks be taken.

Very well, the High Order will provide aid. Please inform Valennia that she can count on us for this fight.

The Windshapers are almost wholly to blame for everything that has happened. Their refusal to change has damaged our ability to save ourselves from our current peril. They speak in absolutes and treat assumptions and superstitious hope as fact.

Do you know who else deals only in absolutes? The Al'Aketh. 

I for one do not intend to let blind adherence to dangerous beliefs doom our people. If it weren't for the threat of the cult, I'd march our mages over to the other side of Valanaar and wipe the Windshapers out.

npc:252476.text: It is vital that we learn more about what the cult is planning, and with the turncoat dead, the information may have died with him...

npc:252800.text: The Windfield Orchard has seen better days...

npc:253002.text: <The Skyborne lying before you is unconscious.>

npc:253004.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.
Winds tidings. What can I help you with?
I hope that your interruption is for a good cause. I was in the middle of some important work.

npc:253372.text: <This cultist is dead. Upon close inspection, you notice that he seems to be clutching something to his chest, almost as if he was protecting it.>

npc:253474.text: What are you looking for, citizen?
Which class trainer are you looking for?
You'll want to head over to the Hall of Arms on the north side of Valanaar.

npc:253576.text:
Most of the cultists at the Sanctum of Storms seem to have come out to respond to our attack. I never would have expected this to go so well. This was almost too easy...

I think that the Windshapers and High Order have made their push. Valennia should be with them. You should head inside and find her. We'll stay here and keep watch while Valennia and the others finish what they came here to do.

npc:253590.text: <Valennia is severely wounded and is barely holding on to consciousness.>

npc:253847.text:
Lorthuna is performing some sort of ritual up there. She may be trying to bring down the wards!

The help we sent for has not yet arrived, but we'll just have to manage with what we have. When you are ready, let me know and we'll go confront her.

npc:254151.text: The Nightclaw do not take kindly to reckless intruders. Tread carefully while in Shadowgale, $c.

You've earned a degree of trust amongst the Nightclaw, $c. We don't have much to offer you as a reward, but we have managed to scavenge a number of crafting plans from the ruins of Ban'aethal.

The magesmiths of Ban'aethal were widely regarded to be the best artisans in all of the Skyborne Isles. The Nightclaw are naturalists, not crafters, so these records are of little use to us.

Continue to prove yourself to be a valuable ally, and I would make these secrets available to you.

npc:254345.text: Another Herbalist, hmm. I doubt your skill is as great as my own so perhaps I can train you in a few proper techniques.

npc:254411.text: You've come for training in order to pass it on to your pets?

npc:255940.text: Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?

npc:256930.text: Desperation? Hunger? I'm not exactly here doing this because I like robbing and murdering. I lost my home, had nowhere to go, and I don't much care to shave my head and worship some imaginary wind god, so I became a bandit. The rest is obvious.
Killed a peacekeeper and stole some windstones.
Largely, yes. The thing we all have in common is that we have nowhere else to go and that we prefer thieving over enslaving ourselves to some insane cult.

Most of my outfit did. Displaced from the ground falling out from under our feet. Some came from other islands entirely. I came from the city of Shen'dramar, on the big island. Well, what used to be the big island, I suppose.

My family and I managed to get on one of the last skycutters out of there before the entire island broke apart. We thought that Zephras would save us. Well, it didn't. They are all long dead and now I'm here, awaiting execution.
Why bother denying it, the constable already passed her judgement. No point lying.

npc:257003.text: I don't get too many Skinners in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.

npc:257005.text: I hope that your interruption is for a good cause. I was in the middle of some important work.
Winds tidings. What can I help you with?

npc:257006.text: I don't get too many cooks in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.

Cooking on Zephras may seem difficult to the untrained eye, but I enjoy the creation of every dish. Even though our dwindling home is lacking many of our traditional kaldorei ingredients, it has been fun to create new variations of the recipes of our ancestors.

I hope that no matter where the winds take you, these recipes remind you of home.

npc:257007.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.

npc:257008.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.

npc:257019.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.
Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?

npc:257020.text: I hope that your interruption is for a good cause. I was in the middle of some important work.
Winds tidings. What can I help you with?

npc:257021.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.
Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?

npc:257022.text:
You might think that just because we live on a floating island, there would be no need for miners like me. After so many thousands of years, however, we still manage to dig up a lot of interesting things.

It's almost like there's some invisible force, constantly creating new mineral deposits every so often. That's magic for you though, right?

Regardless, if you need training as a miner, then I'm your shen'dorei.

npc:257024.text: I don't get too many Skinners in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.

npc:257036.text: Welcome to the Bank of Valanaar. We can secure your belongings and valuables here should you so desire. Do you wish to access your deposit box?

npc:257065.text: Do you seek the blessings of the Windlord?

npc:257554.text: <The gaze of the ranger standing before you is fixed on the enormous anchor pylon in the distance.>

npc:258130.text:
<Before you lies the corpse of Jorel Windsinger.

Deep lacerations are cut into his legs, and lightning burns scorch his fur.

It is clear he put up a fight before succumbing to his wounds.>

npc:258568.text: Best deals in all of Stormwind my friend, won't find any better. Now, what can I help you with?

npc:259012.text: All of the skyborne islands became destabilized and began to move apart a few years ago. If that wasn't bad enough, now large pieces of Zephras are beginning to fall away. It's hard to imagine your home falling into the sky, but that is my reality now.

npc:259013.text:
<Before you lies a skyborne; his body is mangled and bruised but still recognizable. It is clear he met a gruesome end while attempting to flee.

It appears that all of his belongings are still on his body, and a half-filled crate nearby lies spilled on the ground.>

npc:259084.text: Wind's greetings, friend. I've been authorized to offer fellow Skyborne quick passage to the city of Stormwind. Please feel free to utilize this portal at your leisure.

npc:263113.text: It can get boring up here, you know. I can only annoy that stuffy wretch Halaan so much before even that gets old.

npc:265944.text: Cooking is a life long pursuit and I see we share the same passion!
I can teach you how to cook!

npc:267008.text: They named it Bandarion Keep. I wonder what Garek would make of that?

npc:267009.text: Be careful, $c. There are cultists nearby.

npc:2704.text: Heya mon.  You come right place learn how ta wield a new weapon.

npc:271465.text:
Greetings, $c. Are you in need of arms?

I was trained by Antarion of Ban'aethal, using secrets handed down from the ancient master magesmiths of Kalimdor.

You'll find no finer weapons on Zephras Isle than mine.

npc:272526.text:
Yes, I am the renowned trader who magnanimously fed the uh, starving... children...? ...of the Undercity during the recent war with the Scourge. Yes, I am the visionary businessgob and logistical genius who single-handedly armed the resistance and allowed our Dark Lady to found her nation of smelly corpses... um, I mean, "Forsaken."

Yep, I'm him. Glix Xizzix. I'd be happy to sign an autograph. For a small fee, of course.

What am I doing here running a barbershop, you ask? Well I got one word for you, bub--diversification. You've got to keep your revenue streams diversified!

npc:275269.text: Board here for transport to Dalaran City, nestled in the Alterac Mountains.

npc:275491.text:
Ah yes, he mentioned that an agent of the High Order would be arriving in Stormwind soon. He asked me to draft instructions for you.

<Randal hands you a neatly sealed note.>

This should give you all the information you need. You are in for quite the journey, $n. I wish you luck on behalf of Stormwind and the Alliance.
Greetings, citizen. How may I help you today?

npc:276067.text:
It's my job to get the Paladins of Bandarion Keep set up with proper arms and armor. It's not much, but it's honest work.

I've got a thing or two for sale as well, should you need gear.

npc:276170.text: I am Belanaa Windveil and I am an agent of the High Order here on Azeroth. If you'd like to make a donation of cloth to our organization, we would be most grateful.

npc:3296.text: Looking to learn how to use a new weapon?  Find Sayoc and Hanashi inside Arms of Legend in the Valley of Honor.

npc:3310.text: You haven't lived until you've looked down on the world from the back of a wind rider.

npc:4551.text: How may I be of service?

npc:4556.text: Greetings, and welcome.  I am not very good at smiling, but trust me; I am happy to serve you.

npc:4565.text: It is wise that you humble yourself before me $n in your desire for more warlock knowledge.

npc:5688.text: Rest your weary bones for a spell.

npc:5750.text: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.

npc:5759.text: I can train you in First Aid techniques.

npc:6497.text: What do you want, $c? I'm running late, and my employer doesn't look kindly on tardiness.

npc:6739.text: Rest your weary bones for a spell.

npc:6741.text: Rest your weary bones for a spell.

npc:7683.text: Welcome to Blue Moon Odds and Ends, $c.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

npc:9566.text: My brother said we could make great money with this trade route, but he didn't tell me I would be the one living on this side. If you come back this way on the Zeppelin, could you bring me something to eat? They sell some of the finest meat in Orgrimmar, and I sure could use something that didn't die weeks before it stopped moving.

object:581822.text: <A dusty but high-quality satchel lies in the dirt.>

npc:1938.text: The Kirin Tor did not heed my warnings! The Alliance is a sham. Arugal is a reckless fool.

npc:2121.text: Information... With our scouts and agents, we control the flow of information in Lordaeron. Scourge movements, their holdings, all underneath our watchful eyes...

npc:257944.text: I cannot believe we were taken by surprise by the Al'Aketh. They have never been hostile to us before, but with their ambush they injured many of my kin. I swear I will get revenge for the fallen and wounded druids of my den. Mark my words, they will pay.

accept.text: As my understanding of Arugal's magic grows so does my disdain for the hapless fool.  I am close to completing my research on his so called remedy.$b$bMy knowledge will be complete when I learn what enchantment is causing the strange behavior going on in Pyrewood Village.  By day, the peasants appear to be Human.  But when the sun goes down the townsfolk turn into Moonrage Worgen.$b$bI need to draw energy from the enchanted shackles Arugal cast on them.  Bring to me six enchanted Pyrewood Shackles, $n.

complete.text: Your persistence is commendable.  With the knowledge you helped me gather, Arugal will fall and his reckless magic shall be undone.  Cheers to you, $N.

objectives.text: Bring 6 Pyrewood Shackles to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: Have you secured the Pyrewood Shackles yet, $N?

complete.text: Very good. Your efforts do much to keep the Scourge at bay. A commendation will be sent to my superior, Executor Zygand.
Ah, this venom will do perfectly, $N.  Everything else has been added to my concoction and boiled down.  Finally, I am ready to try this new deadly agent!

progress.text: Do you have some venom from a Vicious Night Web Spider yet, $N?  It's the final component I need in order to test my experiment.

complete.text: Captain Perrine's death will undoubtedly please The Dark Lady.  You have performed your duty well, $c.

accept.text: We are still at war and the Scarlet Crusade grows in strength.  The report Executor Arren sent me indicates Scarlet Crusaders have been raiding from the ruined tower in southeastern Tirisfal near the Balnir Farmstead under the command of Captain Vachon.$b$bKill Vachon along with 5 Scarlet Friars. It should prove to be a devastating blow to the Crusade!

complete.text: Captain Vachon's death will slow down the Scarlet Crusade's advancement in Tirisfal quite a bit.  But other threats loom.

objectives.text: Executor Zygand in Brill has commissioned you to slay Captain Vachon and 5 Scarlet Friars.

accept.text: Scarlet Crusaders have been raiding from the ruined tower in northern Tirisfal, past Faol's Rest.  According to the information we have, a ruthless commander named Captain Melrache is in charge of this evil crew.$b$bI am entrusting you now with a special and dangerous mission.  Slay Melrache and his two bodyguards, in the name of The Dark Lady.

complete.text: You have done extremely well, $c.  With ruthless fighters like you conquering in the name of The Forsaken our race is one step closer to defeating Arthas once and for all.  I have a good feeling about you, comrade.

objectives.text: Executor Zygand in the town of Brill wants you to assassinate Captain Melrache and his two bodyguards.

complete.text: Varimathras would be proud.  You serve your leaders well, $c.

progress.text: Have you collected 10 Scarlet Insignia Rings yet, $c?

complete.text:
Your actions struck a telling blow against the Scourge.  And your victory will not go unnoticed - not by the Forsaken, nor by our enemies.

Continue the struggle as we all do, $N, and one day we will drive the Lich King himself from Azeroth!

progress.text: Time is not a luxury we have, $N.  With each passing hour, the Scourge's hold on Tirisfal Glades grows more firm.

accept.text: Lady Sylvanas has charged Varimathras with the conquering of the human and dwarven lands to the south.$b$bBut that fool, Arugal -- charlatan of Dalaran and now cursed beast of Shadowfang Keep -- let his reckless magic wreak havoc with the strategic stronghold of Silverpine Forest.$b$bI need someone skilled in the ways of combat to help clean up Arugal's mess.  Prove yourself to me by killing 5 Moonrage Whitescalps.  The wretched beasts can often be found just off the road, down the hill below.

complete.text: You have served me well, $c.  It is obvious to me that you will be a worthy aide to me as I prepare to rid Silverpine Forest of Arugal's curse.

objectives.text: Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher wants you to kill 5 Moonrage Whitescalps.

accept.text: How Arugal gained acceptance within the Kirin Tor is beyond me.  His spell-casting knowledge seemed as transparent as a blown glass bauble.$b$bWhat's important now is learning exactly what magic Arugal used so that I can turn it against him and secure Silverpine Forest for the Dark Lady.$b$bArugal first stayed at the wheat farm just north of the bridge.  One of the Deathstalkers reported seeing some spellbooks but could not secure them.  Retrieve for me the spell labeled Remedy of Arugal from those books.

complete.text: This is precisely the spell I was in search of, $c.  If your dedication to The Dark Lady's cause remains infallible you will find you have quite a future amongst The Forsaken.

objectives.text: Retrieve the Remedy of Arugal for Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: Before I know what we are dealing with here, $c, I need to study the spell known as Remedy of Arugal.  Bring it to me now or I shall be forced to find myself a worthy servant.

accept.text: After examining Arugal's work my worst suspicions were confirmed.  The old hack was not qualified to clean chamber pots in Dalaran let alone represent the Kirin Tor in its most dire hour.  Fools!$b$bArugal used enchanted items to reinforce his weak magic.  I need to examine these items first hand.  Travel forth and slay Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls until you have collected enough of their enchanted shackles for my research.  The foul creatures have been seen to the north and east.

complete.text:
I hope I can acquire enough energy from such a limited sample.  Perhaps I should have had you get more shackles.

Nonetheless, you showed great skill in collecting these, $c.

objectives.text: Bring 6 Glutton Shackles and 3 Darksoul Shackles to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: I will need 6 Glutton Shackles and 3 Darksoul Shackles before I can assess the situation and devise a final solution for Arugal.  Now heed your bidding and slay Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls until you have what I need.

accept.text: It will indeed take me longer than I had thought to uncover the dark secrets behind the enchantments Arugal was using.$b$bBut in the meantime I need you to take care of a slight problem our Darkstalkers have discovered.  It seems that Arugal let his magic spread to the Deep Elem Mine in the hills to the southeast.$b$bThe mine would prove to be quite a resource for Varimathras's advance.$b$bI want you to behead the tainted foreman of the mine, Grimson the Pale.  With his death, the mine shall be ours.

complete.text: Most excellent.  The mine will provide superb resources for our forces as we spread throughout Silverpine and into Azeroth.

objectives.text: Kill Grimson the Pale and bring his head to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: Has Grimson the Pale been slain?  Varimathras will not be pleased if we ignore his bidding.

accept.text: My brother Quinn and I were tasked to recon Silverpine Forest and report to High Executor Hadrec.  But we didn't get far -- when moving through this farm we were attacked by the ghoul Ivar the Foul.$B$BWe escaped from Ivar, but he seriously mauled Quinn.  He's healing from the potion you gave him, but Ivar may return before Quinn recovers.$B$BKill Ivar so Quinn will have time to heal.  Ivar is usually in the barn yonder, waiting for my guard to drop.

complete.text:
Ah, thank you.  You have my gratitude, $N.

And I will include you in the report I make to my superiors.

objectives.text: Kill Ivar the Foul, and bring Ivar's Head to Rane Yorick at the Ivar Patch.

progress.text: Have you killed Ivar the Foul?  If you won't do it for me and my brother, then do it for the Forsaken.

accept.text: My brother Quinn was badly hurt by the ghoul, Ivar the Foul, and I don't know if he will heal properly without alchemical aid.  Although I am not an apothecary, I do know that our apothecaries can make healing potions from the discolored hearts of worgs.$B$BGather such hearts and take them to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher to the south.  Then return here with the potion.$B$BYou can find plenty of worgs between here and Malden's Orchard to the east.

complete.text:
<Renferrel takes the hearts.>

It is troubling to hear our Deathstalkers have failed their mission.

Let us hope that these failures are rare.

I'll give you the potion in a moment.

objectives.text: Gather 3 discolored worg hearts and bring them to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: My time is short, $c, for the Dark Lady has charged me with a grave task.

accept.text: Here is the potion to aid in Quinn Yorick's recovery.$B$BNow if you will excuse me, I have very important work to continue...

complete.text:
<Quinn takes the potion and drinks it.>

<A few moments pass in suspenseful silence.>

objectives.text: Bring Quinn's potion to Quinn Yorick at the Ivar Patch, north of the Sepulcher.

progress.text: My sister told me you were here to aid us.  Is that true?

accept.text: Our initial scouting reports of Silverpine show the rot hides have a base at an old farm to the north, the Dead Fields.  We have sent small assaults against them, but each time they are reinforced by the banshee Nightlash, who uses her magic to rout our forces.$B$BWe want Nightlash destroyed.$B$BGo to the Dead Fields and assault the rot hides.  If you don't see Nightlash then kill the rot hides until she appears, then defeat her.$B$BHer essence will turn to dust.  Bring me that dust as proof.

complete.text:
I heard of your successful raid against the rot hides, $N, and this essence is proof of Nightlash's death.

The Scourge have lost ground this day.  Your value to the Forsaken grows.

objectives.text: Kill rot hide gnolls at the Dead Fields.$B$BWhen Nightlash appears, kill her.$B$BBring the Essence of Nightlash to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: Have you defeated Nightlash, $N?  Our success against the rot hides depends on her destruction!

accept.text: $n, we've discovered a new hive for the Scourge: the Decrepit Ferry.  The ferry lies east of the Sepulcher, and is heavily patrolled by rot hides and other undead.$B$BThere must be a reason for the Scourge's occupation of the area.  Go to the Decrepit Ferry and find out why the Scourge are there.

complete.text:
Heaped within this boat is a pile of wrapped corpses.  And looking east across Lordamere Lake, an opposing dock on Fenris Isle can be seen.

The fate of the corpses must lie on Fenris Isle.

objectives.text: Go to the Decrepit Ferry.$B$BSearch for the reason the Scourge are there.

accept.text: Among the corpses a hand protrudes, unwrapped.  It is the hand of a woman, pockmarked from the plague but relatively fresh.  $B$BOn the hand is a ring.  Removing the ring and inspecting it reveals an engraving:$B$B"For Deliah"

complete.text:
You say that this ring was worn by a woman, recently killed?

The only nearby source of such a body would be the mass graves in Tirisfal.  The Rot Hide Gnolls must be taking those corpses to Fenris Isle!

objectives.text: Bring Deliah's Ring to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: $N.  You return, so I assume your investigations bore fruit?

accept.text: If you want to find the husband or beloved who gave Deliah her ring... then speak with Magistrate Sevren in Brill.  He should have records of recent deaths and, with luck, can discover who Deliah is.$B$BBut I wouldn't hope.  Whoever gave her the ring is probably dead.  Or if he's undead he probably no longer cares about Deliah.

complete.text:
A Deliah did live in Brill not long ago.  She was buried in the mass grave but if what you say is true, then the Rot Hide Gnolls must have stolen her body and taken it to Silverpine.

The Rot Hides, like all the Scourge, must be destroyed.  I trust you are taking steps to make that happen.

objectives.text: Bring Deliah's Ring to Magistrate Sevren in Brill.

progress.text: Hello, $N.  What brings you back to Brill?

accept.text: Deliah had a husband, Raleigh, who now dwells in the Undercity.  If the Deliah who lived in Brill is the one who owned this ring, then Raleigh will know.$B$BRaleigh is in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity.

complete.text:
Yes, this ring was my wife's.  Her fate was the fate of all who fail to endure these harsh times.  I feel nothing for her death, nor for the story you tell of her body's abduction.

Such feelings have long since grown cold within me.  But desire does still burn in my dead heart, $N.

Desire for revenge.

objectives.text: Bring Deliah's Ring to Raleigh.

progress.text: Do I know you?

accept.text: Before we launch an assault on Fenris Isle, we must determine who is behind the rot hide gnolls.  Our apothecaries believe their origin lies within the strange fluid that flows through their bodies.$B$BGo to Fenris Isle, east of the Decrepit Ferry, and collect rot hide ichor from the gnolls you find there.  Bring it to Apothecary Renferrel, stationed outside the Sepulcher.

objectives.text: Bring 8 bottles of rot hide ichor to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher.

complete.text:
Ah, how good of Apothecary Johaan to send his research.  With so many new developments here in Silverpine, I nearly forgot about the findings coming out of Lordaeron and Tirisfal Glades.  Which reminds me, I need to get those samples off to the Necropolis soon.

But you must excuse my rambling.  Extend your stay in Silverpine, $N.  We could use an able bodied $c like you around here.

progress.text: What business do you have with me, $c?

accept.text: Arthas's numbers are overwhelming. But with a New Plague we could eradicate both the Scourge Army and the Human infestation once and for all.$b$bMy studies have proven that spider blood combined with a toxin derived from a grizzled bear heart results in a deadly elixir. Collect samples from the spiders in the Skittering Dark to the northwest and from the bears wandering throughout Silverpine Forest. Deliver the reagents to Master Apothecary Faranell of the Royal Apothecary Society in the Undercity.

complete.text: How good of Apothecary Renferrel to send you to me, $N.  These samples will indeed prove useful to the cause.  I will begin studying their toxic and contaminable properties at once.

objectives.text: Collect 6 Grizzled Bear Hearts and 6 samples of Skittering Blood and deliver them to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

progress.text: Hail, $c.  What business do you have with the Royal Apothecary Society?

accept.text: You can be of further service to the Royal Apothecary Society, $n.$b$bWhen Arugal cast his wretched magic on the forest, he cursed one of our most promising members, Apothecary Berard.  Now a mindless servant of Arugal, Berard is useless to us.  But his findings might prove to be of worth.  He was studying an ancient plague that killed off all the aquatic life in Lake Lordamere ages ago.$b$bRetrieve Berard's Journal from his study in the Pyrewood Village Inn and take it to Apothecary Renferrel.

complete.text: Apothecary Berard's journal!  Why you are quite brave, $N.  Now let's see what Berard was up to before he went mad. . .

objectives.text: Retrieve Apothecary Berard's journal from Pyrewood Village and take it to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: I see you are back, $N.

accept.text: According to Berard's Journal the moss from Lake Skulkers and Creepers might prove useful for our quest to brew a new plague.  Those beasts dwell on the islands in Lake Lordamere to the east.$b$bHe also mentions a very rare Hardened Tumor that he discovered on a Vile Fin murloc.  Apparently the tumor is so rare Berard was only able to obtain one.$b$bCollect samples of the moss as well as the rare hardened tumor and take them to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

objectives.text: Bring 6 samples of Lake Creeper Moss, 6 samples of Lake Skulker Moss and a Hardened Tumor to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

accept.text: You got here just in the nick of time, $n!$b$bThe Pyrewood Council will be returning any moment.  Arugal has other matters to tend to in the keep.  He uses the Council as mere puppets to keep the mindless minions of Pyrewood under his control.  But I believe that without the guidance of the Pyrewood Council, the sons of Arugal will turn against their master.$b$bI cannot handle them all by myself.  I need you to help me.  Together we can lay waste to the Council for Lady Sylvanas.

complete.text: You fought like a true disciple of the Dark Lady, $N.  With the council dead, perhaps we can gain control of this town once and for all and drive Arugal from Shadowfang Keep.  I salute you!

objectives.text: Help Deathstalker Faerleia kill the Pyrewood Council.

accept.text: As you may know, the town of Ambermill remains a source of human opposition, mainly through the support they receive from the wizards of Dalaran.$b$bI don't know what their plan is, but for them to show interest in a backwater village like Ambermill indicates that it must have some greater importance.$b$bThey've been shipping crates by the wagon from Hillsbrad. Many of those supplies end up at a small camp north of Pyrewood Village. Retrieve the contents of a crate and return them to me.

complete.text:
<Prying open the lid of the crate, you find an assortment of carefully-packed objects. On the top of the crate lies a bundle of maps, yellowing with age, that appear to depict Silverpine Forest and other parts of western Lordaeron.

Underneath the maps is a mysterious-looking magical pendant.>

objectives.text: Retrieve the contents of one of the Dalaran wizards' crates. You will find Pyrewood Village to the south.

accept.text: <You quickly remove the pendant from the crate and replace the lid.>

complete.text:
Maps and this... pendant, hm? Interesting.

It is obvious that the Dalaran wizards are interested in Ambermill for some purpose, but still, their aim is hidden to me.

Perhaps Dalar will know something of their use.

objectives.text: Bring the strange pendant to Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: Have you learned anything useful, $N?

accept.text: Dalar is attempting to locate the source of the wizards' spellcasting. For now, we'll have to slow their progress in any way we can...$b$bThe conjurers, mages and protectors are no doubt carrying the pendants. Remove and retrieve them.$b$bTake the main road south and the eastern fork into Ambermill.

complete.text:
Dalar has found that the weaving is quite far along, despite the setback.

A wizard of great power is guiding the magic energy. He must be stopped quickly.

objectives.text: Obtain 8 Dalaran Pendants for Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: We must hurry, their plans must not come to fruition, or we may lose our hold on Silverpine Forest.

accept.text: Take the pendant to Dalar Dawnweaver, perhaps he can shed some light on the wizards' plans.

complete.text:
Interesting, more machinations of the Kirin Tor, it would seem. This is a powerful artifact. It was used frequently by powerful wizards of the Kirin Tor to channel magical energies.

That they are delivering so many to Ambermill indicates that they must be undergoing a project of some magnitude.

I will see if I can pierce their shields and ascertain their intent.

objectives.text: Take the rune-inscribed pendant to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: Yes, $c? What is it?

accept.text: Of course! How could I have forgotten?$b$bAmbermill was one of the sites earmarked by the Kirin Tor, noted because it houses a dormant ley energy node. The wizards must be planning to reactivate the node and use its energies for some greater purpose.$b$bWe cannot allow this to happen...$b$bIt will take a great amount of power to activate the area's ley energies, we can stall them by taking the pendants away from the wizards.$b$bRelay this information to Allister, he will decide a course of action.

complete.text:
Ill news you bring, $N. If Dalar is correct--and I've no reason to believe he isn't--we must move quickly.

I must confer with him on our plan of attack. But in the meanwhile we will have to delay their progress.

objectives.text: Speak with Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher.

accept.text: According to the Deathguard, another one of those foolish Dwarven Mountaineers has just been captured.  The Deathguard likes to use the cellar of the Gallows End Tavern as a holding cell until prisoners can be "properly" dealt with.$b$bWhy don't you go see how the Captured Mountaineer enjoys this special drink I made for him?  It contains a subtle hint of what The Dark Lady has planned for the rest of Azeroth.

complete.text: Ah, a drink at last.  I'm sure it's no Rhapsody Malt but I'll take anything to whet the old whistle at this point.

objectives.text: Bring Johaan's Special Drink to the Captured Mountaineer.

progress.text: Why if I had my trusted rifle you'd be as good as dead, $C.  Just wait until the Steam Tank Brigade arrives to rescue me!

accept.text: I have received reports that a group of undead are holing up to prepare for an attack against us. Armed with this information, we can turn the tables and attack them first, nipping their little plan in the bud.$b$bUnfortunately, my information is spotty, at best. They are reported to be hiding in a location known as Beren's Peril. The exact location is unknown, but it appears to be a cave in the hills, near a pocket of Dalaran wizards.$b$bI trust your resourcefulness. Find them, and put them down.

objectives.text: Locate Beren's Peril, then kill 6 Ravenclaw Drudgers and 6 Ravenclaw Guardians, then return to Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher.

accept.text: Valdred, once my good friend, was my wife's murderer.  Although I am incapable of grieving, I do yearn for revenge.  If you kill Valdred and bring me his cursed hands, then I will reward you.$B$BI last heard he was at the Greymane Wall in southern Silverpine, trying to flee into the kingdom of Gilneas.

objectives.text: Kill Valdred Moray.$B$BBring his hands to Raleigh Andrean in the Undercity.

progress.text: King Anduin has placed great importance on learning, and thus has provided funds for making copies of various tomes and writings available to the public. It's very simple. You bring me a library scrip, and I can give you a copy of one of the available books.

complete.text:
You have done well, $N. Now, I will impart to you the spell used for summoning the voidwalker.

The power that it unleashed upon you is now yours to command. Use it wisely.

progress.text: I expect to hear of your success, $N. Not meeting my expectations will be the least of your worries, however, should you fail.

accept.text: Many denizens of the Legion bestow gifts on their followers as you may well know. Some of these gifts the Dark Lady feels would be better off in her hands than in the hands of those with... lesser vision.$B$BA sect of the Shadow Council hidden in caverns below Orgrimmar known as the Searing Blade are a prime example. The Lady tells me that members of the Searing Blade have come into the possession of two powerful spell books--she would like to "borrow" these books from them. You will get them for her.

objectives.text: Bring the books Spells of Shadow and Incantations from the Nether to Varimathras in Undercity.

accept.text: Executor Hadrec asked me to take stock of our equipment at the Sepulcher.  With the Scourge, and worse, lurking in the woods, he doesn't want the Deathguards to lack gear they might need.$B$BI found that we are, in general, well stocked, but we do need more weapons to replace those lost in the field.$B$BHere is a requisition order of what is needed, for the weapon dealer Gordon Wendham in the Undercity.  Take the order to our bat master, Karos Razok, and speak with him about transport to the Undercity.

complete.text: Ah, an order for supplies.  You will want to take this to the Undercity, no doubt.  And quickly, for the Sepulcher must not be left under stocked.

objectives.text: Bring Podrig's Order to Karos Razok.

progress.text: You appear to be on official business...

accept.text: I have placed the Sepulcher's supplies into this crate.  If you have already visited the Sepulcher and spoken with their bat master, then you may ride a bat back to him.$B$BSpeak with the Undercity's bat master, Michael Garrett.  He can provide you with a bat to the Sepulcher.

complete.text: This crate must reach the Sepulcher in Silverpine?  That is easily done; our bats fly there daily.

objectives.text: Bring Gordon's Crate to Michael Garrett.

progress.text: If you must travel a long distance, then a bat is your best option.

accept.text: One of my bats can take you to the Undercity, for a small fee.  Speak with me again when you are ready so that we may arrange your transport.$B$BYou will find Gordon Wendham in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity.  That is the same quarter where my bat will land.

complete.text: An order from the Sepulcher?  Very well.  It is an honor to serve those who serve our Dark Lady.

objectives.text: Buy a bat ride to the Undercity from the bat master Karos Razok, then take Podrig's Order to Gordon Wendham in the Undercity.

progress.text: I keep my weapons in top condition.  They are cleaned and ready for use.

accept.text: The bat master in the Sepulcher is Karos Razok.  If you have already met him, then I can give you a bat to fly back to him.$B$BOur bats will always fly to the Undercity, but to travel to more remote locales their rider must first visit the area and speak with its bat master.$B$BYou have met Karos in the Sepulcher, so you may now fly bats there.  Speak with me again when you are ready.

complete.text:
Good work, $N.  These weapons will ensure our Deathguards don't get caught unprepared.

You have done a valuable service for our Dark Lady.

objectives.text: Buy a bat ride to the Sepulcher from the bat master Michael Garrett, then bring Gordon's Crate to Deathguard Podrig in the Sepulcher.

progress.text: $N, you return.  Do you have our supplies from the Undercity?

We are currently accepting donations for wool cloth.  A donation of sixty pieces of wool cloth will net you full recognition by Stormwind for your generous actions.  Our stores are such on wool that we would only need sixty pieces from you total; we should be able to acquire enough from others in the realm to support our drive.

If you have the sixty pieces of wool cloth on you and are ready to donate them, I'm able to take them from you now.

We are currently accepting donations for wool cloth.  A donation of sixty pieces of wool cloth will net you full recognition by the Undercity for your generous actions.  Our stores are such on wool that we would only need sixty pieces from you total; we should be able to acquire enough from others in the realm to support our drive.

If you have the sixty pieces of wool cloth on you and are ready to donate them, I'm able to take them from you now.

accept.text:
I wouldn't dare to question the effectiveness of Apothecary Renferrel's formulae, however I would be lying if I said that the potion made any noticeable difference.

Along the shore of Lake Lordamere are a swarm of murlocs, and of note, murlocs have eyes. I suspect the apothecary's willingness to try new things is suppressed by his recent obsession with hearts. Bring him a few.

If my choice is to inevitably die a second death or have Renferrel kill me for questioning his methods, I choose the latter.

complete.text:
The potion didn't work? Of course it didn't work. You brought me insufficient hearts. The recipe clearly calls for six. You brought three.

However, I confess I hadn't considered applications for murloc parts until now...

<Renferrel takes the eyes.>

I can afford to sacrifice a few of my own hearts to get your Deathstalker's strength back.

objectives.text: Gather 3 murloc eyes and bring them to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher.

progress.text: Oh. You're back?

accept.text:
Here is the new potion to aid in Quinn's recovery, made with love extracted from six whole hearts.

Now, please excuse me before your presence necessitates more paperwork.

complete.text:
<Quinn takes the potion and drinks it.>

Yes, I can feel it working. I will soon be able to travel.

You have done me a great favor, $N.

objectives.text: Bring Quinn's potion to Quinn Yorick at the Ivar Patch, north of the Sepulcher.

progress.text: You return! I was beginning to come to terms with devolving into a ghoul.

accept.text:
It's my husband Edward...

He has not returned from his weekly journey to the graveyard in the Lordaeron ruins. Our son was lost when Arthas razed the city, and my dear Edward is still filled with guilt and sorrow that we never found his body. I've tried to warn him against searching those overrun ruins, but he refuses to give up. I try not to worry, but it's been days.

There are things there I cannot contend with but if you are willing, I need to know the fate of my husband.

objectives.text: Investigate the disappearance of Edward Heartweaver in the Ruins of Lordaeron.

accept.text:
Look at you, bright eyed and ready for adventure! We need all the help we can get here in Thendal Village and your arrival is most welcome. I imagine you are brimming with nerves for what is to come. After all, you only get to come of age once in a lifetime.

Go, seek out our village leader Rorian the Dayseeker at the entrance to the greatfather tree just west of here. He will get you started on your journey.

complete.text:
Gale's greetings, $N. I am honored to bestow your coming of age relic today as you are recognized for the potential you bring to the shen'dorei. Our people have faced great hardship and persecution in our complex history.

Today you are given this relic which is one of many held by those before you. Someday when your ashes are scattered to the winds it will pass to another to continue our tradition.

As you take this relic with you know that the winds of home will be with you wherever you travel.

objectives.text: Speak with Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Grove.

accept.text:
We live in times of great uncertainty for our people. We face unprecedented challenges that may require bold solutions, but we also must contend with the ordinary and mundane here in Thendal Grove. Take, for example, the recent unsustainable rise in the vuldren population.

The vuldren are a vital part of our ecosystem. However, imbalances must be corrected to maintain the delicate harmony that all creatures in Thendal Grove share.

Head east and cull some of the vuldren there.

complete.text:
Thank you for your service to Zephras, young $c.

The vuldren are typically quite docile, but the animals that call Zephras home can sense when the magic on the winds is out of balance, which can lead to dangerous and unpredictable behavior if left unchecked.

objectives.text: Slay 8 Vuldren Juveniles in Thendal Grove.

accept.text:
One of our rangers recently reported an infestation of cirrusflies here in Thendal Grove. 

Cirrusflies can be dangerous if the swarm is allowed to grow too large, so please head to the eastern end of the Grove and exterminate as many as you can.

complete.text: Judging by the amount of bug entrails covering you, this must be quite the infestation.

objectives.text: Slay 8 Pesky Cirrusflies in Thendal Grove.

accept.text:
If the forest is as thick with these insects as it sounds, simply killing the workers won't be enough.

Go deeper into the forest and find the queen. She'll be close to the hive and surrounded by bigger and more aggressive soldiers, so be careful.

Put her down and return here when it's done. That'll be one less problem to think about around here.

complete.text: Excellent work, $N. You'd make a fine ranger if this whole "adventurer" thing doesn't work out for you.

objectives.text: Destroy the Cirrusfly Queen in Thendal Grove.

progress.text: Cirrusflies aren't to be underestimated. They might not seem dangerous, but you have to watch out for the bigger ones. The bigger they are, the meaner!

accept.text:
Ever since our elemental benefactors left us, it seems that we are simply moving from one unrest to another. The problem we face now is that the manifestations of the winds near the standing stones to the northeast are agitated.

Not truly self-aware like the sentient wind spirits that once lived here, these simple sprites respond in kind to forces, emotions, and intentions of the creatures around them. 

My apprentice Yala Windwatcher went to observe them. Seek her out and discover what she's learned.

complete.text: Rorian sent you? Good. I could use your aid.

objectives.text: Speak to Yala Windwatcher in Thendal Grove.

accept.text:
The Al'Aketh cult is a blight upon this island. These cultists are surely the ones responsible for agitating the simple wind sprites that reside here and turning them violent.

Regrettably, we'll need to disperse these roiling winds here before they harm someone. We also need to send a clear message to the cult that they are not welcome in the grove.

Will you lend me your aid, $c?

complete.text: It pains me to shed shen'dorei blood here in the grove, but we do what we must.

objectives.text: Slay $2oa Roiling Winds and $1oa Al'Aketh Converts in Thendal Grove.

accept.text:
You've done enough here, $c. I'll stay and clean up any stragglers down there.

Head back to the Village and tell Rorian about the cult's presence. He will not be pleased.

complete.text:
This is most troubling, but unfortunately unsurprising. We've been aware of the cult's movements for some time, but we've been content to watch from afar. Their agitation of the wind spirits near the standing stones is a clear escalation on their part.

You've performed a difficult but necessary service for Thendal Grove, $N. Thank you.

objectives.text: Bring word of the Al'Aketh to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Grove.

accept.text:
Rorian informed you that I've been watching you. I now offer you a test of resolve. However, be warned--it will send you into great danger.

Go to the caves to the south. Thin out the ursera's numbers there, and find their matriarch, one the rangers call "Urs'anah". Put her down and bring me proof of her demise. Once you have done that, you will have taken an important step on your path.

complete.text: Very well done. You've felled beasts and laid low cultist interlopers. You have shown great promise but your path must soon take you beyond the relative safety of Thendal Village.

objectives.text: Slay 8 Ursera Scavengers and collect the head of the den mother, Urs'anah in Thendal Grove.

progress.text: What I ask of you is not easy, but you must be prepared for much greater challenges if you are to survive long enough to be of service to Zephras Isle.

accept.text:
You may not realize this but everything you've done has been a trial of sorts. A test for what is to come for you. It's a big island out there, and Zephras needs spirited young adventurers such as yourself if we are to survive the trials our people face.

The one called Aetheen of the Gales is one of the leaders of our people here on Zephras Isle, and she has been watching you. She has a task that you must complete. Speak with her to learn more.

complete.text:
Rorian has told me much of you. I am likely unknown to you, but I am a member of the Council of Elders here on Zephras Isle. I've come to read the flow of the winds here in Thendal Grove. I'm also here to assess young shen'dorei such as yourself that are coming of age.

So tell me, are you ready to take your next step? Are you ready to serve Zephras Isle?

objectives.text: Speak with Aetheen of the Gales in Thendal Grove.

accept.text:
One of the most pervasive threats on Zephras Isle is the Al'Aketh Cult. They are religious zealots devoted to the worship of the supposed elemental ruler of Skywall, Al'Akir the Windlord. They are brutal, single-minded, and their power and ambitions are growing more deadly by the day.

Your path will soon take you to Shen'dar Village to the south. Present yourself to Constable Aonda when you arrive. The cult threatens Shen'dar and they are in need of aid. Tell Aonda that I sent you.

complete.text: Aetheen sent you, then? I'll confess, you don't look like much to me, but Shen'dar Village won't turn down willing aid, much less aid sent from Elder Aetheen herself.

objectives.text: Report to Constable Aonda in Shen'dar Village.

accept.text:
The ursera den to the southwest is rapidly becoming a problem. Just last week the rangers had to kill an adolescent ursera who wandered too close to the village and attempted to attack a boy playing near the base of the elder tree in the center of the village.

We were fortunate that the boy escaped with his life. Hunger and desperation makes these beasts too dangerous to be left unchecked. Go south and put the scrawniest among the ursera down. Bring me their claws as proof when it is done.

complete.text: Well done, $c. The Rangers of the Grove are in your debt.

objectives.text: Collect 6 Scrawny Ursera Claws from Scrawny Ursera in Thendal Grove.

progress.text: The ursera have grown far more aggressive of late. I wonder what has changed to cause this shift in behavior?

accept.text:
Well hello there, $n! Want to play a game?

All you've got to do is step up on that ledge... then jump! Use your innate ability to walk on the air to slow your fall and see how far forward you can float.

The rules are made up and the points don't matter, but you get bonus points if you can land right in front of Rorian the Dayseeker and startle him! He won't like it but I'll certainly get a good laugh if you can get him all worked up! Hah!

complete.text:
How many times do I need to tell Myriaal not to encourage others to make reckless usage of our skyborne gifts!

That being said, I suppose that a little bit of practice in the relative safety of the village is... acceptable.

In the future I'd simply suggest you to use your ability judiciously. You do not want to exhaust your magic thoughtlessly and then not be able to use it when you truly need it.

objectives.text: Jump from the top of the watchtower in Thendal Grove and use your Walk on Air ability to slow your fall.

accept.text: While you were away dealing with our vuldren problem, our resident hunter trainer--Tai'ree Farsight--left this note for you. You can find her just over yonder near the center of the village. Read the note then seek her out.

complete.text:
The way of the $c is fraught with danger, and only those with the keenest senses and quickest reflexes can thrive in the wilds. I look at you and I am reminded of myself when I stood before my mentor, so many years ago. I believe that you have what it takes, but in the end that is up to you alone.

Speak with me again if you wish to take your next steps.

objectives.text: Read the Scribbled Note and then speak with Tai'ree Farsight in Thendal Grove.

progress.text: <Tai'ree nods at you curtly.>

accept.text:
As if bandits and mad cultists weren't enough, the hills are thick with prideclaws as well right now. They are starting to encroach on the village borders and growing bolder by the day. It's only a matter of time before someone's pet or child is taken. It would be a mercy for us to cull their numbers now rather than after some tragedy occurs.

Bring me a dozen or so of their pelts. I can turn them into all sorts of goods that will be of aid to the village.

complete.text: I didn't say it wouldn't be a dirty job, did I?

objectives.text: Collect 10 Prideclaw Pelts from the Prideclaws in Shen'dar Highlands.

progress.text: If you ask me, I think Prideclaws are actually kind of cute. From a safe distance... and while standing behind someone holding a sword, of course.

accept.text: A flock of Hippogryph have recently established nesting grounds southeast of Shen'dar Village and they've been wreaking havoc on travelers on the road. I need someone to head down there and thin them out for us.

complete.text: Well done, and quickly too. Not too bad at all.

objectives.text: Slay 8 Hippogryph Youths, 6 Hippogryph Protectors and a Hippogryph Matriarch in the Shen'dar Highlands.

accept.text:
There's a cave not far to the north, hidden behind a waterfall. It's well known to me that there's a group of bandits that are operating out of that cave. They were a problem for us before the cult arrived, but now they are a real terror. I can't spare the people to go and clear them out, unfortunately.

I need you to go there and take care of them for me. Kill as many as you can, and if possible, take out their leader, the one they call "Badwind" Bennic. That cave is dangerous, so be careful.

complete.text:
With the bandits dispersed, that is one less problem for us to deal with. Though I confess that now I worry that any bandits who survived may turn next to the cult for protection, further bolstering their increasingly alarming numbers.

Still though, we'll take the victories where we can get them.

objectives.text: Kill 10 Highlands Bandits and their leader, "Badwind" Bennic in the Shen'dar Highlands.

accept.text:
The faithful of Al'Akir grow ever stronger with each eager new recruit like yourself. As you can see, our strength gives form to the storm itself!

Normally I'd send you straight to Skypriest Aanders for assessment, but he is occupied at present receiving a guest at the inn on the north side of town. Please avoid that place for now. An unshaven recruit like yourself in the presence of such a guest would be inappropriate.

For now, just don't get in anyone's way.

complete.text:
Lorthuna herself was there? She's the leader of the whole damned cult!

If they are making a move on Shen'dar Village and the western watchtower, we've got to be ready. What is strange is... why the watchtower?

The Village I can understand, but the tower? It doesn't have much strategic significance, other than as a minor lookout post.

Regardless, we will be prepared for them. They'll find that highlanders aren't as easy to catch flat footed as they might think.

objectives.text: Look around Falaath Village to learn about the cult's intentions in the Shen'dar Highlands.

accept.text:
It gladdens my heart that you wish to serve Al'Akir. Our current trials as a people stem from our own complacency. We grew prideful and took the bounty of the winds for granted. The stagnation that followed is the reason the spirits of the wind abandoned us.
